relevance_note: Biochemical study of plasma lipoproteins of named patients with familial LCAT deficiency ("M. R., a 23-yr old nonlipemic female, and L. G., a 38-yr old lipemic male"); no LCAT variants are printed.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short script assembled the JSON from hand-written values. Five in-scope people: M. R., L. G., I. S., A. A. (studied here) and A. R. (sister of M. R., described only in the Discussion with nephrotic syndrome, rising plasma TG, loss of renal function and dialysis; included as a relative with individual-level facts; no disease label is given to her). No LCAT gene or variant is mentioned anywhere (1973 biochemical paper), so the variants table is empty. Group statements in Methods ('None of the patients was obese...', 'All had slightly reduced concentrations of serum albumin... and moderately increased concentrations of urine protein') and Discussion ('none of the patients studied here has the nephrotic syndrome, all have moderate proteinuria') were applied to the four named patients of the study (M. R., L. G., I. S., A. A.) as 'inferred from group statement'; not applied to A. R. Hypertriglyceridemia checklist: observed for L. G. and I. S. and excluded for M. R. from the sentence that VLDL (d < 1.006) TG was elevated in I. S. and L. G. but not M. R., plus M. R. 'does not have hyperlipemia'; A. A. is only called 'lipemic' and left not reported. A. R. plasma TG increased then decreased to almost normal; recorded observed. Reduced cholesteryl ester fraction from 'In each patient all subfractions contained abnormally small amounts of CE' referring to L. G., M. R. (Tables VI, VII) and I. S. (Table VIII). Lipoprotein numbers in Tables I-VIII were not converted into features (no per-person statement of abnormality beyond the text). The background count 'Six patients ... discovered in Scandinavia' is not tied to these individuals, so ethnicity_or_country is not reported and n_patients_reported is null. Publication year is not printed (only received/revised dates 1972/1973), so year is null. Ages given ('23-yr old' etc.) are ages at the time of study, recorded as age at last evaluation. OCR is garbled in places (e.g. 'oyn tn in n tns'); no values were taken from garbled text. No contradictions found.
